8.1 — Boss Design: Reuse & Brainstorm

Between Thanksgiving and Winter Break you are building the Boss Fight on your own. There is no pre-built Boss prefab in the project — instead, you already have every building block inside Assets/Scripts/. Today you brainstorm multiple boss concepts by remixing existing parts, pick one you can actually finish in two weeks, and sketch it before opening Unity.

The Reuse Catalog: What You Already Built ~15 min

Before inventing scripts from scratch, inventory the working prefabs and C# classes already inside your repository. A great Unity boss is often two or three familiar pieces combined in a dramatic room:

Existing PieceWhat It Already DoesHow to Reuse It on a Boss
EnemyController Walks patrolPoints, tracks target in range, has health, ChangeHealth(), and drops itemDrop inside Die(). Scale it up into the main boss body, speed up patrol phases, or drop the victory key/portal prefab on Die().
TurretController + Projectile Fires fireballPrefab tagged E_Fireball every timeBetweenShots seconds using Shoot(). Mount turrets as boss weak points, corner cannons, or flying orb phases that track the player automatically.
Platform Moves along wayPoints via MoveTowards() and parents the player via SetParent(). Build moving boss battlegrounds, elevator shields blocking shots, or a rising escape platform when defeated.
Spawner Calls Instantiate() to drop prefabToSpawn into the scene. Convert the trigger into a timed wave or phase-2 minion spawner inside the arena.
Lever + SceneSwitch Fires onLeverOn UnityEvents or moves the player to the next scene cleanly. Lower a boss barrier, trigger hazard lights, or warp back to a victory screen once the boss drops the exit.
StatManager Holds health, coins, HUD text, and jumpsRemaining across every scene; Die() reloads the arena cleanly. Tracks survival through the boss room and resets the entire arena cleanly if the player runs out of health.

Socratic: Remixing Before Writing

  1. Look at the table above: which three existing components can create a multi-phase boss fight before you write a single new script?
  2. PlayerController.Update() switches gravity on automatically via Start() in every scene except Overworld. If you put the boss in its own Boss scene, what does the player get for free without editing scene detection?
  3. In EnemyController, destroying a boss on Die() already instantiates itemDrop. Why does dropping a reward, portal, or SceneSwitch object beat teleporting silently the millisecond health <= 0?
In the Editor: Brainstorm & Spec on Paper (~35 min) ~35 min

Step 1 — Divergent brainstorm (10 min): Sketch three completely different boss concepts in three boxes. Do not pick your first idea immediately — push yourself to try one stationary multi-turret machine, one mobile patrolling stalker, and one arena-puzzle boss (platforms + levers + hazards).

Step 2 — Pick one and write the build spec (25 min): Choose the idea that has the clearest silhouette and can reach a playable prototype in your very next class:

  1. Arena layout: draw a side-view map showing floors tagged Ground, any ladders or moving Platform lifts, turret mounts, and player safe spots.
  2. Player verbs: say how BOTH KeyCode.E melee (attackBox) and KeyCode.Space ranged (PlayerProjectile) interact with the boss, plus jumping and double jumping.
  3. Two phases: describe Phase 1 (calm, teaches the tell) and Phase 2 (under 50% health — faster timer, second turret, moving lift turns on, or minions appear).
  4. Win & Lose loop: what spawns or opens when the boss hits zero health, and how does StatManager.Die() reset everything cleanly if the player loses?
Two-week scope rule: pick ONE boss room, ONE clear health bar or visual damage tell, and AT MOST TWO distinct attacks or phases. Over-ambitious cutscenes and six untested phases leave nothing playable for friend playtesting next week.

Socratic: Defending the Design

  1. From your three brainstorms, why did you reject the other two — and which single mechanic from your chosen idea is riskiest to build first?
  2. Sketch the attack tell: what does the player see or hear half a second before damage happens so getting hit feels fair rather than random?
  3. Where in this fight do both KeyCode.E melee and KeyCode.Space fireballs matter (or why does one stay risky while the other stays slow)?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Brainstorm three distinct boss concepts that reuse existing game scripts and prefabs
  • Select one realistic two-week scope and sketch the arena, platforms, and hazard placements
  • Specify how the player damages the boss, how the boss escalates in Phase 2, and how victory triggers
  • Commit and push your spec notes before opening prototyping
